title: Stop fbm octaves aligning on the integer lattice
why: fbm doubles frequency exactly and noise2 is value noise, so the x-gradient vanishes on every integer line: median 1.8e-6 there against 0.35 elsewhere. Anything that differentiates a field inherits that grid.
what: In core/rand.js fbm, multiply frequency by 2.17 per octave (Texturing & Modeling 3rd ed., p. 88) or rotate each octave. Add a test that compares |d/dx| on integer lines with elsewhere, a mutation that restores x2, and remove the KNOWN DEFECT comment on fbm.
notes:
Measured with 2.17: 0.28 on integer lines against 0.32 elsewhere (docs/knowledge/imported-sources.md §18.1). This changes every picture that uses fbm (contours, drift, packing) and every seed anyone kept, so the user must accept that before it closes. Pinned fbm values in tests/rand.test.js will move: update them deliberately, never by loosening a check. Findings document: docs/knowledge/imported-sources.md — moved out of the repository on 2026-09-19, so the doc field can no longer point at it.

LACUNARITY is 2.17 and tests/negative.js breaks it back.

title: Add gradient noise to the stochastic source
why: Value noise has a zero derivative across its own lattice lines under any fade that is flat at its ends; gradient noise does not. A field layer that takes gradients or curl needs it.
what: Add an addressed 2D gradient noise (Perlin-style) beside noise2 in core/rand.js, with gradients picked from a fixed table so it stays arithmetic-only and exact in every engine. Test that its derivative on lattice lines is not near zero and that two named fields are independent.

Keep the addressed contract: the gradient at a cell comes from R(name, "grad", cell(i, j)), no stream. No sin or cos, so it stays exact across engines (docs/decisions/decisions.md §024.5). title: Add a WebGPU preview backend for per-pixel field art
why: Per-pixel fbm costs 0.54 s a frame at 1080p and 2.12 s at 4K on this CPU: 8.5 minutes for a 240-frame 4K film. For art whose output is the field itself, at video resolution, that is the bottleneck.
what: Evaluate field art on the GPU for previews only; the CPU stays the reference renderer. Deferred until a piece needs per-pixel field output at video resolution.

title: Stop the mutation suite copying 40 MB it does not test
why: tests/negative.js copyDir skipped only node_modules and .git, so every mutation copied the whole tree. Measured 2026-09-19: 40.4 MB per copy, of which 33.2 MB was .claude (the agent worktrees, each a checkout of this same repo) and 6.75 MB was out/. The source the suite reads is 0.38 MB, so 82 copies moved 3.5 GB to test 0.38 MB. This entry previously claimed the suite mutated the working tree in place; it does not -- copyDir writes only into a temp dir, and an mtime check across a full run confirmed nothing under the checkout moved.
what: Copy only what a mutation run reads. runSuite executes node --test tests/*.test.js, so the copy takes core, examples, tests, tools and package.json and nothing else, filtered at the tree root only. An allow list rather than a deny list, because the deny list could not see docs/ arriving. Print the per-mutation size at the start of a run so the next bloat is visible.
notes:
Distinct from entry 031, which is about the suite COPYING .claude/worktrees (the reason a run takes minutes). This one is about where the mutations land. Evidence and the mtime list were in docs/repository-consolidation.md section 4, deleted 2026-09-20 with the rest of that document; the copy rule and its reasoning now live in tests/negative.js.
